note: Internal-observer GDPR checklist for a source repository. decision_mode routes each check: 'auto' = decided deterministically by evaluate.mjs from the repo scan (files, dependencies, code patterns); 'llm' = bounded judgment over found documents/code excerpts (schema-validated); 'manual' = organizational facts not derivable from code (signed contracts, exercised procedures). Presence-style 'auto' checks detect existence only — adequacy/truthfulness is noted as manual in the rationale.

checks.title: Privacy policy / notice document present in repo
checks.obligation: A controller must provide transparent information about processing; a public-facing project should ship/maintain a privacy notice.
checks.repo_observable: A privacy policy/notice file or page exists in the repo (PRIVACY.md, privacy-policy.*, legal/privacy, locales privacy strings).
signals: privacy route/template in a web app
checks.pass_criteria: A privacy notice document is present and tracked in the repo.
fail_indicators: no privacy notice anywhere in the repo

checks.title: Privacy notice covers the Art. 13 mandatory contents
checks.obligation: The notice must state controller identity/contact, purposes + legal basis, recipients, retention, data-subject rights and the complaint right.
checks.repo_observable: The text of the privacy notice found in the repo can be read and checked for the Art. 13 elements.
checks.pass_criteria: All Art. 13 mandatory elements are present in the notice text.

checks.title: Records of Processing (ROPA) maintained
checks.obligation: Controllers/processors must keep records of processing activities.
checks.repo_observable: A record-of-processing / data-inventory / data-map document exists in the repo (presence only; adequacy is a manual review).
checks.pass_criteria: A ROPA/data-inventory document is present. Its adequacy requires manual review.
fail_indicators: no records-of-processing artefact in the repo

checks.title: Data Processing Agreement (DPA) artefact present
checks.obligation: Engaging a processor requires a contract with the Art. 28(3) mandatory terms.
checks.repo_observable: A DPA / data-processing-agreement template or reference exists in the repo (presence only; signed contracts are manual).
checks.pass_criteria: A DPA artefact or subprocessor list is present. Signed contracts require manual review.
fail_indicators: no DPA / subprocessor documentation despite third-party processors in deps

checks.title: DPIA artefact present for high-risk processing
checks.obligation: A data protection impact assessment is required for high-risk processing.
checks.repo_observable: A DPIA document exists in the repo (presence only; whether a DPIA was actually required/performed is manual).
checks.pass_criteria: A DPIA artefact is present where high-risk processing is plausible. Necessity is a manual judgement.
fail_indicators: special-category data handled but no DPIA artefact

checks.title: Consent-management tooling present where non-essential cookies/trackers are used
checks.obligation: Non-essential cookies/trackers require prior opt-in consent; a web app using them should ship a consent mechanism.
checks.repo_observable: A CMP/consent library appears in dependencies when analytics/marketing SDKs are also present.
checks.pass_criteria: If non-essential trackers are present, a consent-management mechanism is also present.
fail_indicators: analytics/marketing SDKs in deps but no consent tooling

checks.title: Non-essential processing is gated behind consent in code
checks.obligation: Analytics/marketing must execute only after a valid opt-in; code must not fire trackers unconditionally on load.
checks.repo_observable: Consent-gating logic around tracker initialisation can be read in the code excerpts.
signals: tracker init wrapped in a consent check
no unconditional gtag/fbq/analytics init at startup
checks.pass_criteria: Tracker initialisation is conditioned on a recorded consent state.
fail_indicators: analytics initialised unconditionally at app start
no consent check around tracker code

checks.title: No secrets or credentials committed to the repo
checks.obligation: Appropriate technical measures must protect personal data; committed secrets are a serious confidentiality risk.
checks.repo_observable: Committed secret material is detectable (a real .env, private keys, cloud keys, long inline tokens).
checks.pass_criteria: No secret material is committed; .env is gitignored and only .env.example is tracked.

checks.title: Passwords hashed with a strong algorithm
checks.obligation: Credentials must be protected with state-of-the-art measures; weak/absent hashing is non-compliant.
checks.repo_observable: Hashing usage is detectable in code: bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 (good) vs md5/sha1/plaintext for passwords (bad).
checks.pass_criteria: Passwords use bcrypt/scrypt/argon2; no md5/sha1/plaintext for credentials.

checks.title: Personal data is not written to logs
checks.obligation: Logging personal data widens the attack surface and breaches confidentiality/minimisation.
checks.repo_observable: Log statements referencing PII variables are detectable in source.
checks.pass_criteria: No log statements emit personal data or secrets.

checks.title: Cookies set with Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite
checks.obligation: Session/auth cookies carrying identifiers must be protected against theft/leakage.
checks.repo_observable: Cookie-setting code can be inspected for Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite attributes.
signals: res.cookie/set-cookie with httpOnly:true, secure:true, sameSite set
checks.pass_criteria: Cookies that carry identifiers set Secure, HttpOnly and a SameSite policy.

checks.title: Dependency manifest + lockfile present (vuln management)
checks.obligation: State-of-the-art security includes managing known-vulnerable dependencies.
checks.repo_observable: A dependency manifest and a committed lockfile exist.
checks.pass_criteria: A manifest and a lockfile are committed, enabling reproducible, auditable dependencies.
fail_indicators: dependencies declared with no lockfile committed

checks.title: Encryption of personal data in transit and at rest
checks.obligation: Encryption/pseudonymisation appropriate to risk should protect personal data.
checks.repo_observable: TLS enforcement and at-rest encryption configuration can be judged from config/code excerpts.
signals: HTTPS/TLS enforced (HSTS, forceSSL, secure transport config)
checks.pass_criteria: Personal data is encrypted in transit and, where appropriate, at rest.

checks.title: Personal-data inventory from data models/schemas
checks.obligation: A controller must know what personal data it processes (the basis for minimisation, retention and rights).
checks.repo_observable: Personal-data fields are detectable in models/schemas/migrations/ORM entities.
checks.pass_criteria: Personal-data fields are enumerated for review (inventory). This is informational, not pass/fail.
fail_indicators: large amounts of PII with no corresponding documentation/inventory

checks.title: Data minimisation — collected PII appears necessary
checks.obligation: Personal data must be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purpose.
checks.repo_observable: The inventoried PII fields can be judged against the apparent purpose of the project.
signals: PII fields collected vs the stated/likely purpose
checks.pass_criteria: Collected PII fields plausibly map to a legitimate purpose; no obvious over-collection.
fail_indicators: collecting sensitive fields with no apparent need

checks.title: Special-category data handling (Art. 9)
checks.obligation: Special-category data (health, biometric, race, religion, sexual orientation, etc.) requires an Art. 9 condition.
checks.repo_observable: Special-category terms are detectable in models/code.
checks.pass_criteria: No special-category data, or its presence is flagged for an Art. 9 lawful-condition + DPIA review.
fail_indicators: special-category data processed with no DPIA/Art. 9 basis evident

checks.title: Data export / portability mechanism present
checks.obligation: Data subjects can access their data and receive it in a portable format.
checks.repo_observable: An export/download/portability endpoint or handler is detectable in the code.
checks.pass_criteria: A data export/portability mechanism exists in the code.
fail_indicators: no access/export mechanism for user data

checks.title: Data erasure / account deletion mechanism present
checks.obligation: Data subjects have the right to erasure ('right to be forgotten').
checks.repo_observable: An erasure/account-deletion endpoint or handler is detectable in the code.
checks.pass_criteria: An erasure/account-deletion mechanism exists in the code.
fail_indicators: no deletion mechanism for user data

checks.title: Rights mechanisms are adequate across access/rectify/erase/port
checks.obligation: The controller must facilitate exercise of all applicable data-subject rights.
checks.repo_observable: The detected rights handlers can be judged for coverage and completeness from code excerpts.
signals: coverage of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection
checks.pass_criteria: The implemented rights mechanisms reasonably cover the applicable rights.

checks.title: Data storage/region configured outside the EEA
checks.obligation: Transfers to third countries require adequacy, safeguards (SCCs/BCRs) or a derogation.
checks.repo_observable: Cloud/storage regions in config reveal where personal data is likely stored/processed.
signals: region tokens us-east-1/us-west/ap-/asia-/non-EEA GCP/Azure regions in config/IaC
checks.pass_criteria: Personal-data storage is in the EEA, or non-EEA regions are backed by a valid transfer mechanism.
fail_indicators: non-EEA region configured for personal-data stores with no transfer safeguard noted

checks.title: Third-party SDKs implying non-EEA processing
checks.obligation: Sending personal data to non-EEA SaaS/SDKs is a transfer requiring a mechanism and disclosure.
checks.repo_observable: Dependencies on US/non-EEA analytics, marketing and cloud SDKs are detectable.
checks.pass_criteria: Non-EEA processor SDKs are inventoried and covered by transfer mechanisms + disclosure.
fail_indicators: non-EEA SDKs receiving PII with no transfer mechanism/disclosure

checks.title: Data retention / deletion logic present
checks.obligation: Personal data must be kept no longer than necessary; storage limitation must be implemented.
checks.repo_observable: Retention/TTL/purge logic is detectable (TTL indexes, expiry fields, scheduled deletion jobs).
checks.pass_criteria: Retention/expiry/purge logic exists for personal data.
fail_indicators: personal data persisted indefinitely with no retention/purge logic

checks.title: Retention periods are defined and bounded
checks.obligation: Retention periods (or criteria) should be defined per data category.
checks.repo_observable: Retention config/docs can be judged for defined, bounded periods.
checks.pass_criteria: Bounded retention periods or clear criteria are defined.

checks.title: Third-party processors inventory from dependencies
checks.obligation: Each processor handling personal data must be known and governed by an Art. 28 contract.
checks.repo_observable: Third-party processor SDKs/services are detectable in dependencies and integrations.
checks.pass_criteria: Processors are inventoried for DPA coverage review (informational).
fail_indicators: processors used with no subprocessor list / DPA artefact

checks.title: Signed DPAs exist for each processor
checks.obligation: A binding Art. 28(3) contract must exist with each processor.
checks.repo_observable: Not derivable from code — the existence of signed processor contracts requires internal/legal review.
signals: N/A from the repo — manual contract review required
checks.pass_criteria: Flagged for manual review; cannot be confirmed from the repo.

checks.title: Age-gate / parental-consent where children may be targeted
checks.obligation: Information-society services offered to children need age verification / parental consent below the applicable age.
checks.repo_observable: Age-gate / date-of-birth / parental-consent logic is detectable in code where relevant.
signals: age-gate / minimum-age / dateOfBirth validation / parental-consent / COPPA references
checks.pass_criteria: If the service may target children, age/parental-consent handling exists. Otherwise N/A.
fail_indicators: evidently child-directed product with no age handling

checks.title: DPO / privacy contact documented
checks.obligation: Where a DPO is designated, their contact must be published; a privacy contact should be reachable.
checks.repo_observable: A DPO/privacy contact is detectable in repo docs (SECURITY.md, README, privacy notice).
checks.pass_criteria: A privacy/DPO contact is documented in the repo.

checks.title: Breach-notification procedure documented
checks.obligation: Controllers must notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours and, where high-risk, affected data subjects.
checks.repo_observable: An incident/breach runbook may exist in the repo, but readiness/exercise of the procedure is a manual/organizational fact.
checks.pass_criteria: Flagged for manual review; readiness cannot be confirmed from the repo.
